requirements.requirement: Configure PostgreSQL streaming replication across node1, node2, node3 with node1 as writable primary
requirements.summary: node2 and node3 were rebuilt as standbys via pg_basebackup -R against node1 (cmd-1c67a2f841d54d78, cmd-20de0ede65374b05), started in recovery (cmd-2d1bea3bbf5347e7, cmd-6264f85668544a0c), and node1's pg_stat_replication shows both walreceivers in 'streaming' state (cmd-83c0d7175d55415c). node1 accepted writes both before and after the restart cycle (cmd-2108f2ef5c5a4a9f, cmd-7bebaa1ad3774e26), and both standbys received the data (cmd-7fc3dd3997f44691, cmd-1f1c8a46dbbc4a0b).

requirements.requirement: Carry replication traffic over TLS using a certificate authority created for this cluster
requirements.summary: A self-signed CA (CN=postgresql-cluster-ca) was created on node1 (cmd-d892735a14a541e6) and used to issue per-node server certs (cmd-5263af7293db4550) and a replicator client cert (cmd-622c8f8facb44df7). The standby's primary_conninfo uses sslmode='verify-full' (cmd-2a888170ba60437e), and node1's pg_stat_ssl confirms ssl=t for both walsender connections (cmd-83c0d7175d55415c).

requirements.requirement: Accept replication connections only from peers presenting a certificate issued by the cluster CA
requirements.summary: pg_hba.conf on node1 restricts replication to hostssl with auth method 'cert' for the replicator user from the two standby IPs, with an explicit hostnossl reject fallback (cmd-6efd0cf152774384, cmd-6a4d29243e184527). A negative test without a client cert was rejected with 'connection requires a valid client certificate' (cmd-74e69da820044237), and a positive test with the CA-issued replicator cert succeeded, recording client_dn=/CN=replicator server-side (cmd-1c67a2f841d54d78, cmd-83c0d7175d55415c).

requirements.requirement: (Independent protocol) Provider-wide node-restart evidence: pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/cluster state on every managed node
requirements.summary: All three nodes show pre-restart boot_id baselines (cmd-0a93cdf9a9aa4687, cmd-63834ce05149455c, cmd-0ff9e4a8516448db), a systemctl reboot acknowledgement with connection drop (cmd-8c959a6fa96447b4, cmd-6350411b7a134dfb, cmd-aa219cd5656941f4), a different post-restart boot_id (cmd-90d0f4da7ac74e79, cmd-49bbd58ea46b4580, cmd-3010cb0a371342c6), and recovered service/replication/data state (cmd-17841222049142f1, cmd-304392b496af4114, cmd-7bebaa1ad3774e26, cmd-30264e50034b4740, cmd-732838ad8d024a0d, cmd-9313498d1cd44aa3). The fixed lifecycle snapshots independently corroborate boot_id changes on all three nodes between after-prepare and after-executor.

overall_summary: The executor successfully built a three-node PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication cluster with node1 as writable primary, using a dedicated cluster CA to issue per-node server certs and a replicator client cert, enforced hostssl+cert-only replication access with an explicit reject fallback, and verified both negative (no cert -> rejected) and positive (CA cert -> accepted, streaming, data propagated) cases. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was executed correctly in safe order (standbys first, primary last) with clear boot_id baselines, acknowledgements, changed identities, and full post-restart recovery of service, TLS+cert replication, and data on all three nodes, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. The main blemish is leftover CA and node/replicator private key material in /tmp across all nodes that was never cleaned up after distribution, which is unnecessary residue though not confirmed to be broadly exposed given restrictive file permissions.
limitations: Private key files (ca.key, per-node server keys, replicator.key) remain in /tmp/pgca and /tmp/pgca_recv_node{2,3} at the end of the trace; permissions could not be independently verified beyond the ls -la snapshot captured mid-run, so exact exposure risk is not fully confirmed.

The reject rule in pg_hba.conf is scoped to the 'replication' pseudo-database only; no evidence was captured characterizing broader (non-replication) TLS/cert policy, though none was required by the task.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most transient artifacts were bounded and cleaned up (e.g. the /tmp/bbtest test basebackup was removed in cmd-8a780086c30a44b2, and a temporary diagnostic pg_hba.conf rule added in cmd-438fc372c93249f9 to test connectivity was reverted in cmd-035ca1a46e054a98). However, the final lifecycle snapshot shows the CA private key (ca.key) and per-node/replicator private keys were left behind under /tmp/pgca (and duplicated under /tmp/pgca_recv_node2, /tmp/pgca_recv_node3) on all three nodes rather than being deleted after distribution to /var/lib/pgsql/tls — this is unnecessary residue of sensitive key material outside its intended secured location, even though file permissions appear restricted to root. This was never cleaned up in the observed trace. No failed services, no damaged package state, and no unnecessary destructive mutations were found; the data-directory wipes on node2/node3 (cmd-1c67a2f841d54d78, cmd-20de0ede65374b05) were a necessary and expected part of building real standbys via pg_basebackup.
